questions.stem:
Study the table and answer the questions.

Number of books sold (in hundreds) by five publishers across four months:

Publisher | January | February | March | April
P         |   25    |    30    |  20   |  25
Q         |   40    |    35    |  45   |  40
R         |   15    |    20    |  25   |  20
S         |   50    |    45    |  40   |  65
T         |   30    |    25    |  35   |  30

What is the total number of books sold (in hundreds) by Publisher S over all four months?
questions.explanation: C is correct. S total = 50 + 45 + 40 + 65 = 200 hundred books. Trap: adding only three months gives 135 or 155; 220 comes from double-counting April.

questions.stem:
Table: (same publisher table)

Publisher | January | February | March | April
P         |   25    |    30    |  20   |  25
Q         |   40    |    35    |  45   |  40
R         |   15    |    20    |  25   |  20
S         |   50    |    45    |  40   |  65
T         |   30    |    25    |  35   |  30

What is the combined total sales (in hundreds) of all publishers in April?
questions.explanation: C is correct. April totals: P=25, Q=40, R=20, S=65, T=30. Sum = 25+40+20+65+30 = 180. Trap: using March column instead gives 25+45+25+40+35 = 170; 165 comes from omitting S.

In which month did Publisher Q sell the highest number of books?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Q's monthly sales: Jan=40, Feb=35, Mar=45, Apr=40. March (45) is the highest. The trap is January and April which are both 40 — students may confuse these with the maximum.

Table: (same publisher table)

Publisher | January | February | March | April
P         |   25    |    30    |  20   |  25
Q         |   40    |    35    |  45   |  40
R         |   15    |    20    |  25   |  20
S         |   50    |    45    |  40   |  65
T         |   30    |    25    |  35   |  30

What is the average monthly sales (in hundreds) of Publisher T?
questions.explanation: C is correct. T total = 30+25+35+30 = 120. Average = 120 ÷ 4 = 30. Traps: 27 comes from dividing by 5 months instead of 4; 28 comes from incorrectly summing (e.g., omitting April).

P         |   25    |    30    |  20   |  25

R         |   15    |    20    |  25   |  20
S         |   50    |    45    |  40   |  65
T         |   30    |    25    |  35   |  30

What percentage of total April sales was contributed by Publisher S? (Round to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: B is correct. April total = 25+40+20+65+30 = 180. S April = 65. % = (65/180) × 100 = 36.11% ≈ 36.1%. Trap: 38.9% comes from using 167 as the denominator (omitting T); 41.7% comes from dividing 65 by 156.

What is the ratio of total four-month sales of Publisher P to Publisher R?
questions.explanation: B is correct. P total = 25+30+20+25 = 100. R total = 15+20+25+20 = 80. Ratio = 100:80 = 5:4. Trap: 4:3 arises from rounding or miscalculation; 5:3 comes from using only 3 months for R.

What is the percentage increase in Publisher R's sales from January to March?
questions.explanation: C is correct. R Jan = 15, R Mar = 25. Increase = 10. % = (10/15) × 100 = 66.67% = 66⅔%. Trap: 50% comes from using 20 as base (February); 60% from using 25 (March) as base instead of January (15).

By how many hundreds of books do Publisher S's total four-month sales exceed Publisher T's total?
questions.explanation: C is correct. S total = 50+45+40+65 = 200. T total = 30+25+35+30 = 120. Difference = 80 hundred books. Trap: 60 comes from using only 3 months for S; 70 from misreading the April column for T as 25 instead of 30.

T         |   30    |    25    |  35   |  30

If Publisher P's actual sales in each month had been 20% higher than shown, what would P's total four-month sales (in hundreds) have been?
questions.explanation: C is correct. P actual total = 25+30+20+25 = 100. 20% higher → 100 × 1.20 = 120. Short Trick: a 20% increase on the total is the same as a 20% increase on each month. Trap: 110 comes from adding 10% instead of 20% (or adding just 10 to 100).

T         |   30    |    25    |  35   |  30

The combined January sales of Publishers P and R as a fraction of total January sales (all five publishers) is:
questions.explanation: B is correct. P Jan = 25, R Jan = 15. P+R = 40. Total January = 25+40+15+50+30 = 160. Fraction = 40/160 = 1/4. Trap: 1/5 from dividing by 200 (total for a different month); 1/3 from dividing 40 by Q+P combined instead of the grand total.
